calls.reason: The only May 2026 performance evidence is Anthropic's own internal data (76% success on open-ended tasks), with no independent comparison of promises to results. That isn't enough to say AI broadly failed or met its promises.

His own figures ($44B + $20.25B, or 40% + 18.4%) come to about 58%, not 68%. Exponential View's $110B also removes double-counting, so adding the labs' revenue to their compute spend overstates their share.
An open-ended forecast with no deadline. Anthropic's S-1 shows it still depends on outside capital, but nothing in the packet shows an industry-wide funding failure.
Hedged with 'appears to be'. Anthropic's losses and OpenAI's $122B round fit his point, but Microsoft's $37B AI run rate has no customer split, so 'only real outcome' can't be checked.
No figures show Anthropic's and OpenAI's spending at each cloud provider. Google naming other GPU customers casts doubt on 'only', but doesn't show those customers paid for these GPU models.

SK hynix and Sandisk credit their record sales to AI and datacenter demand and to higher prices, but nothing in the packet shows whether that demand is speculative. 'Entirely speculative' and 'reckless' are judgements.
